propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any future advisory on a pinned version to block all in-flight changes via pip-audit gating, even when those changes did not touch the dependency map.
The Gerrit verify lane should block on an advisory only when the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, or lock files); non-dependency-touching changes should not be blocked.
The scheduled main CI run should block releases on outstanding advisories, with automatic ticket escalation following the heartbeat-canary pattern for dedup and notification.

override-dependencies is the correct instrument to remedy a real advisory blocked by an upstream cap; constraint-dependencies can only narrow and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, not proof an upgrade is impossible.

A documented runbook must guide users away from false-progress moves (uv lock --upgrade-package against a cap, misinterpreting UNSATISFIABLE), name the override mechanism with justification requirements, and state the verification set (uv lock --check, uv sync --locked --extra dev, pip-audit over full environment).

Advisory severity tiers (CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warn, LOW tracked) must apply, with unrated advisories treated as HIGH to avoid silent misses; DB-unreachable flakes remain the only recheckable failures.
